episodes.title: Morning Screen Check
episodes.text: You open the online screen and walk through the steps. The output does not match what it should show. You note exactly what you see.

episodes.title: Building Regression Checks
episodes.text: You sit down to work on your testing program. You add checks for regression and negative paths. You include a check for database impacts.

trial.title: Order the regression work
items: Retest the fixed error
Pick the software scenario to cover
Run the regression checks
Add a negative testing step
trial.explain: You pick the scenario first, then run checks before retesting fixes.

episodes.title: Updating Procedure Notes
episodes.text: You open the test procedure document. You update the same steps so they can be repeated. Same file as yesterday, same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Reporting a Defect
episodes.text: You message the developer about the defect you found.

choice.prompt: The developer asks for the defect details now. What do you send?

options.label: Send clear steps and what you saw
options.outcome: You send the steps and the wrong output. They can follow it and start looking.

options.label: Send a short note with no steps
options.outcome: You send a short note. They write back asking for the steps and screen details.

chat.text: Saw you flagged something on the output screen?
Can you share the steps and what went wrong?

episodes.title: Failed Bug Retest
episodes.text: You retest a bug that was marked fixed. The program function still fails in the same way. You stop and check the content again.

choice.prompt: The retest still fails. What do you do next?

options.label: Document it and report it again
options.outcome: You add fresh notes and send it back. It goes back in line to be fixed.

options.label: Wait and retest later quietly
options.outcome: You wait and try it again later. It still fails and still needs reporting.

options.label: Mark it passed for now
options.outcome: You mark it passed. The problem stays and comes back later.

episodes.title: Logging Bugs Quietly
episodes.text: You open the bug tracking system. You enter the defects with steps and output details. You save each one before you log off.

episodes.title: Checking Morning Charts
episodes.text: You sit down with today's folders. You read each prescription, diagnosis, and chart. You match every name to the plan for the day.

episodes.title: Helping You Settle In
episodes.text: You greet your first patient in the treatment room. You help them onto the table to position them.

choice.prompt: The patient is tense and a little off the mark on the table. What do you do?

options.label: Take time to reposition them accurately
options.outcome: You talk them through each small move. They settle and you line them up to the prescription.

options.label: Keep them where they are to save time
options.outcome: You start out of alignment. You have to stop and set them up again anyway.

chat.text: I'm nervous. Am I in the right spot?
My back hurts if I lie flat too long.
Please tell me what you are doing.

episodes.title: Same Safety Checks Again
episodes.text: You do the same radiation protection checks as yesterday. You check the room, the shields, and your distance. You log it and move on.

episodes.title: Giving the Treatment Dose
episodes.text: You set the machine for the prescribed dose. You aim it at the specific body part listed. You deliver the treatment as practiced.

trial.title: Check Before You Treat
trial.scenario: You have reviewed the prescription and chart. The patient is positioned on the table. The machine is set for a different body part than the prescription lists.
options: Wrong body part is set on the machine
The room lights are too bright
The chart paper is folded
trial.explain: You always match the machine setup to the body part in the prescription.

episodes.title: Running Afternoon Sessions Alone
episodes.text: You run the afternoon sessions on your own. You follow the long-term treatment plan the physician set. You keep each session steady and unrushed.

episodes.title: Name Does Not Match
episodes.text: You check the wristband against the chart and prescription. The names do not match. You pause before touching the machine.

choice.prompt: The identification does not match the chart. What do you do?

options.label: Stop and recheck identification and chart
options.outcome: You hold the treatment. You sort out the correct chart and prescription before anyone is treated.

options.label: Treat anyway since they are next
options.outcome: You risk giving radiation to the wrong person. The session is stopped when the error is found.

options.label: Ask the physician for direction
options.outcome: You wait for clarity. The physician confirms you must not treat until identity is confirmed.

episodes.title: First Chest Image
episodes.text: You walk into the x-ray room and check today's request. You help the patient onto the examining table. You move the machine into place to get a clear view of the chest.

episodes.title: Explaining the Scan
episodes.text: You sit down next to a nervous patient before her scan. You start to explain what will happen.

choice.prompt: She is shaky on the table and you still need to explain the scan. What do you do first?

options.label: Pause and explain in plain steps
options.outcome: You explain the breath hold and how long she stays still. She nods and settles back on the table.

options.label: Start the scan right away
options.outcome: You begin positioning while she is still shaky. She shifts during the scan and you have to stop and calm her.

chat.text: Will this hurt? How long do I have to stay still?
I feel a little shaky up on this table.
Do I need to hold my breath?

episodes.title: Same Safety Checks
episodes.text: You check the lead aprons and shields between patients. You wipe the table and put the shields back in the same spot. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Setting Exposure Controls
episodes.text: You pull up the specification for an ankle exam. You position the imaging equipment over the ankle. You adjust the controls to set the exposure time and distance.

trial.title: Set up the exposure
items: Set the exposure time on the controls
Read the exam specification for the view
Set the distance between tube and patient
Position the imaging equipment over the area
trial.explain: You read the spec first, then position and set time and distance.

episodes.title: Patient Feels Faint
episodes.text: You watch the patient on the table during the scan. His face goes pale and he says he feels faint. You keep watching and get ready to report to the physician.

choice.prompt: He is pale and sweaty on the table. What do you do now?

options.label: Stop and report to the physician
options.outcome: You stop the exam and tell the physician what you see. The physician comes in and checks him while you stay with him.

options.label: Keep going to finish fast
options.outcome: You try one more view while he feels worse. You stop anyway and have to report the faintness and the blurred image.

options.label: Help him sit up alone
options.outcome: You help him sit up slowly and watch him closely. You still report the change to the physician before continuing.

episodes.title: Lead Aprons On
episodes.text: You bring out the protection devices for the last exam. You place a lead apron and shield on the patient and step behind the screen. You check that staff are covered before you expose the image.

episodes.title: Morning Buyer List
episodes.text: You arrive and open your buyer's notes. You look at what they need and what they can pay. You make a short list of homes that fit both.

episodes.title: Daily Status Checks
episodes.text: You sit with your open purchase files. You check the same lender, escrow, and inspection items as yesterday. You write down no change and do it again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Showing The Offer
episodes.text: You sit with the sellers at their table. You lay out the buyer's written offer for them to consider.

choice.prompt: The sellers ask what you think they should do about this offer.

options.label: Read the offer terms back and wait
options.outcome: They reread the price and dates. They tell you they need more time to decide.

options.label: Ask what part worries them most
options.outcome: They point to the closing date. You note it to take back to the buyer.

chat.text: Walk us through the price and dates.
Does the buyer want anything else with the house?
Give us a minute to think this over.

episodes.title: Checking The Contract
episodes.text: You sit down with the purchase agreement. You read each name, date, and address line by line. You fix a small error before it goes out.

trial.title: Find the contract error
trial.scenario: You check a purchase agreement for a buyer and seller. The price and dates match, but the buyer name is spelled wrong on one page.
options: The wrong buyer name on that page
The color of the paper
The time of day you check it
trial.explain: The wrong name must be fixed or the agreement is not right.

episodes.title: Stuck On Price
episodes.text: You stand between the buyer and seller on price. The buyer will not raise the offer and the seller will not lower the price. Both wait for you to carry the next word.

choice.prompt: Neither side will move on price. What do you do next?

options.label: Carry the seller's last price to the buyer
options.outcome: The buyer hears the number and says no. The talk pauses until tomorrow.

options.label: Ask each side about dates or small terms
options.outcome: Both list what dates they can do. You write the answers down for each side.

options.label: Pause the talk for today
options.outcome: Both agree to stop and think. You set a time to talk again.

episodes.title: Closing Papers Ready
episodes.text: You pull together the closing statement and deed. You check that the names and numbers match the purchase agreement. You stack the lease papers ready to sign.

episodes.title: Checking Yesterday's Records
episodes.text: You sit down and open the public records search. You look through sales, leases, and assessments for the street you are working. It is the same screen as yesterday, and it will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Photographing the House
episodes.text: You walk around the outside of the house and take your exterior shots. You step inside and photograph each room in order.

trial.title: Missing Photo Check
trial.scenario: You flip through the photos back at your car. You have the front exterior, the living room, and the kitchen. You have no photo of the back exterior.
options: The back exterior still needs a photo
The kitchen needs another photo
The photos are complete for the report
trial.explain: The report needs both interiors and exteriors to show the property.

episodes.title: Asking About Nearby Sales
episodes.text: You stop by the county office to get land values and nearby sales.

chat.text: Morning. Which block are you pulling today?
I have two sales from last month on that street if you need them.

episodes.title: Working the Value
episodes.text: You sit with your notes and compare this house to the similar properties nearby. You factor in depreciation, replacement cost, and income potential. You work toward one final estimation of value.

choice.prompt: Your two best comparisons point to different values. What do you do now?

options.label: Weight the most similar sale
options.outcome: You base the value more on the closer match and note why in your work.

options.label: Average the two sales
options.outcome: You split the difference and write down why you averaged them.

episodes.title: Missing Sale Record
episodes.text: You search the public records again for a recent nearby sale. The file shows a sale but no price. You need that number to finish your comparison.

choice.prompt: The sale price is missing from the record. What do you do?

options.label: Use another nearby sale
options.outcome: You set that sale aside and use a different sale with a clear price.

options.label: Wait and check the updated record
options.outcome: You pause that comparison and check back when the record is updated.

options.label: Call the county for the price
options.outcome: You ask the county office for the sale price and add it if they confirm it.

episodes.title: Writing the Report
episodes.text: You type your written report at your desk. You state your value estimate and outline the methods you used. You check that it meets appraisal standards before you close it.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Real Estate Investor (flips) — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Real Estate Investor (rentals) — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Planning Morning Sessions
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down with your notes. You look over a needs assessment and list the patient's interests. You draft today's treatment plan around the goals of therapy.

trial.title: Order the plan steps
items: Match activities to the objectives of therapy
Note the patient's interests
Start from the needs assessment
Write the treatment plan to meet the need
trial.explain: You start from the assessment, add interests and objectives, then write the plan.

episodes.title: Teaching Relaxation Breathing
episodes.text: You sit down with a patient one to one. You show a slow breathing and relaxation technique for their anxiety. You practice it together step by step.

choice.prompt: The patient struggles with the pace and looks frustrated. What do you do?

options.label: Slow it down further
options.outcome: You shorten the counts and practice slower breaths. The patient stays with you and finishes the set.

options.label: Switch to gentle music listening
options.outcome: You put on calm music and practice breathing to the beat. The patient relaxes a little and you note the change.

episodes.title: Leading Group Music
episodes.text: You gather five patients in the activity room. You lead a music session to support mood and movement. You play, sing, and keep everyone involved.

episodes.title: Charting After Lunch
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and open the same notes form. You record who came, what they did, and how they reacted. It is the same as yesterday and will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: When Session Stalls
episodes.text: You are mid-session and one patient stops taking part.

choice.prompt: The patient has stopped and wants to quit the activity. What do you do?

options.label: Offer a different art activity
options.outcome: You bring out paper and markers for a simple art task. The patient picks it up and rejoins for the last ten minutes.

options.label: Pause and sit with them
options.outcome: You stop the activity and sit nearby for a few minutes. The patient stays in the room and you record a low participation day.

options.label: End their session early
options.outcome: You walk them back and note the reaction and early stop. You plan to adjust tomorrow's program.

chat.text: I don't want to do this. This isn't helping.
Can we just stop?

episodes.title: Updating Treatment Records
episodes.text: You return to your desk with the afternoon notes. You record participation, reactions, and progress from today's sessions. You adjust tomorrow's programs to fit what you saw.

episodes.title: Explaining the Leave Policy
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open a video call with a new hire. She asks what the parental leave policy actually means for her start date. You pull up the policy and walk through it in plain language.

choice.prompt: She asks if she can start leave early under the policy. How do you answer?

options.label: Read the policy section word by word with her
options.outcome: You read it together and check what the rules allow. She writes down the dates that fit the policy.

options.label: Summarize what the policy allows and offer to follow up
options.outcome: You explain the main points and send her the written policy after. She reviews it and emails her dates.

episodes.title: Filing Hiring Forms
episodes.text: You sit with the stack of hiring forms from yesterday. You check each signature box and file them in order. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Scheduling the Skills Test
episodes.text: You message an applicant to set up her skills test for tomorrow morning.

chat.text: Hi, is the test online? How long does it take?
I can do tomorrow morning if that works.

episodes.title: Reading the New Guidelines
episodes.text: You sit down with the updated EEO guidance after lunch. You read through the ADA notes and mark what changed. You save the summary with your hiring notes.

episodes.title: Test Accommodation Request
episodes.text: An applicant tells you he needs extra time on the test for a disability. The test is scheduled to start in an hour. You pause and check what the ADA rules require.

choice.prompt: The test starts soon and he needs an accommodation. What do you do?

options.label: Pause the test and arrange the accommodation
options.outcome: You delay his slot and set up extra time as allowed. He takes the test later that day.

options.label: Keep the original time but document his request
options.outcome: You note his request and ask him to wait while you check the rules. His test is moved until the review is done.

options.label: Ask what specific accommodation he needs for the test
options.outcome: You listen and write down exactly what he asks for. You compare it to the ADA guidance before rescheduling.

episodes.title: Entering Benefit Choices
episodes.text: You open the benefit enrollment for a new employee. You enter his health plan choice and check the form. You file the signed copy for the record.

trial.title: Benefit Enrollment Order
items: File the signed enrollment form
Explain the plan options to the employee
Collect the signed form
Enter the election in the system
trial.explain: You explain first, then collect, enter, and file the choice.

episodes.title: First Client Talk
episodes.text: You sit down with your first client before the table is warm.

choice.prompt: She waits to hear how you will use her history today.

options.label: Focus the massage for back tension and stress
options.outcome: You explain you will keep the work gentle around the ankle and focus on calming back tension. She nods and lies back.

options.label: Ask one more question about the ankle pain
options.outcome: She tells you it still aches after long days. You note it and adjust where you will work.

chat.text: My lower back has been tight for weeks and work stress is high.
I had ankle surgery last year, does that matter?

episodes.title: Hands On Feet
episodes.text: You settle onto the stool and take her right foot in both hands. You find the sore spot with your thumb and hold steady pressure. You breathe with her and keep the pressure even.

trial.title: Notice what matters
trial.scenario: You are applying finger pressure to a point on the foot. The skin looks fine, the pressure feels steady, but the client says a sharp pain shoots up her leg.
options: Keep holding the same pressure
Ease off and check her pain
Move to the other foot
trial.explain: You stop and check pain first before you continue the work.

episodes.title: Shoulders And Back
episodes.text: Your next client wants full-body care for wellness. You knead along his shoulders and upper back with slow palms. You work the tight muscles until they soften under your hands.

episodes.title: Wiping Down Room
episodes.text: You wipe the table and headrest with cleaner. You refold the towels and refill the oil bottle. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Foot Pain Flares
episodes.text: You are pressing a point on his foot when he winces.

choice.prompt: He looks at you, waiting to know if you will continue.

options.label: Stop the pressure and ask about the pain
options.outcome: You lift your thumbs and ask where it hurts and how bad it feels. He points to the arch and you change your plan for that foot.

options.label: Lighten the pressure and keep working nearby
options.outcome: You ease your thumbs off the sore point and work softly around it. He relaxes a little and says that feels better.

chat.text: Ouch, that spot really hurts right now.
Should we just keep going?

episodes.title: Planning Next Visits
episodes.text: You sit with your last client and talk through what helped today. You suggest two more short sessions using foot pressure work. You write down the plan and hand it to her.

episodes.title: Morning Vitals Round
episodes.text: You arrive on the unit and pick up your list. You sit down by the first bed and take temperature, pulse, and blood pressure. You write each number in the chart.

trial.title: Chart the vitals
items: Write the numbers in the chart
Ask the name and check the wristband
Note symptoms the patient mentions
Take temperature, pulse, and blood pressure
trial.explain: You check who it is before you measure anything.

episodes.title: Morning Medications
episodes.text: You bring the medication cup to the bedside.

choice.prompt: The patient says the pill caused itching before. Do you give it now?

options.label: Hold the dose and check
options.outcome: You do not give the pill and you tell the charge nurse what the patient said.

options.label: Give the dose and watch
options.outcome: You give the pill and stay to watch for itching or rash.

chat.text: That pill made me feel itchy last time.
Should I still take it now?

episodes.title: Same Checks Again
episodes.text: You go room to room with the cuff and thermometer. You record the same numbers you recorded yesterday. You will do it again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Walking After Surgery
episodes.text: You help a patient stand by the bed for rehab. You hold the arm and walk slow steps down the hall. You sit together until the breathing steadies.

episodes.title: A Sudden Change
episodes.text: You see a patient's breathing turn fast and skin turn pale. You recheck the pulse and see it has changed. You need to act on the new symptoms.

choice.prompt: The symptoms are getting worse. What do you do first?

options.label: Call for help and report
options.outcome: You press the call button and report the new breathing and pulse to the nurse in charge.

options.label: Stay and keep watching
options.outcome: You stay at the bedside and keep recording the breathing and pulse every few minutes.

options.label: Record it for later
options.outcome: You write the changes in the notes to hand off at the end of the shift.

episodes.title: End of Shift Notes
episodes.text: You sit at the desk with the charts. You write up medications given and changes you saw today. You sign each page and leave it for nights.

episodes.title: Setting Up Machines
episodes.text: You arrive before the first case and pull the anesthesia machine to the bedside. You check the monitors, suction, and ventilation circuit. You lay out the drugs, fluids, and airway supplies you selected for the day.

trial.title: Set up for anesthesia
items: Connect the monitors and check they read
Lay out airway supplies for intubation
Draw up the anesthetics and fluids you selected
Check the anesthesia machine and suction
trial.explain: You check the machine first, then monitors, supplies, and drugs are ready in that order.

episodes.title: Putting To Sleep
episodes.text: You sit down at the head of the bed and start the anesthetics and fluids you ordered. You place the breathing tube and connect mechanical ventilation. You watch the chest rise and listen for steady air movement.

choice.prompt: The dose is taking effect but the airway looks tight. What do you do next?

options.label: Give a little more anesthetic and reposition before tubing
options.outcome: You adjust the head position and give more drug. The jaw relaxes and you place the tube smoothly.

options.label: Place the tube now as planned
options.outcome: You place the tube now and confirm placement. You stay close and adjust ventilation to settle breathing.

episodes.title: Watching the Numbers
episodes.text: You sit by the monitors and watch pulse, blood pressure, respiration, and urine output. You note skin color and check the ventilator again. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Checking In After
episodes.text: You stand with your awake patient in recovery and check breathing and color. You ask about nausea and shortness of breath. You give ordered fluids and a small adjuvant drug for comfort.

episodes.title: Blood Pressure Drops
episodes.text: You are mid-case when the blood pressure falls and the heart rate climbs.

choice.prompt: Blood pressure is still dropping. Do you push emergency fluids first or give an emergency drug first?

options.label: Open emergency fluids and reassess airway and ventilation
options.outcome: You open fluids and recheck the airway and ventilation. Pressure steadies enough to keep the case safe.

options.label: Give an emergency blood pressure drug now
options.outcome: You give the drug and watch the monitor closely. Heart rate and pressure come back into range.

options.label: Call for advanced life support help while you stabilize
options.outcome: Help arrives and you keep managing airway and drugs together. The team steadies the patient with you.

chat.text: Pressure is 78 over 42 and falling.
Do you want fluids wide open or pressors now?
Tell me what you need, I am right here.

episodes.title: Waking Up Safe
episodes.text: You turn down the anesthetics and let the patient start breathing on their own. You remove the breathing tube once air movement is strong and steady. You stay close, watching pulse, respiration, and pupil response.

episodes.title: Opening Yesterday's Notes
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down at your desk. You open your case files. You check yesterday's notes on services provided and client contacts.

episodes.title: Talking Through Options
episodes.text: You sit down with a client to talk through options and goals.

choice.prompt: The client waits for you to guide the talk. What do you focus on first?

options.label: Ask about their goals for work
options.outcome: You write down the goals they name. You use them to start shaping the service plan.

options.label: Walk through each service option slowly
options.outcome: You explain each service one by one. The client asks questions and marks what sounds useful.

chat.text: I am not sure what kind of work I can still do.
Can we go over what services I can use?

episodes.title: Shaping The Plan
episodes.text: You sit with the notes from the morning talk. You match a rehabilitation plan to the client's aptitudes, education, physical abilities, and career goals. You write the next steps into the plan.

trial.title: Order the plan steps
items: Write down the career goal the client named
List what the client can do physically
Note the client's aptitudes
Note the client's education level
trial.explain: You start with aptitudes and education before you fit the plan to the goal.

episodes.title: Logging Progress Checks
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk and log progress. You mark the same boxes for each client. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Bus Route Falls Through
episodes.text: You get word a client lost their ride to a work site. You call them to talk through the barrier.

choice.prompt: The client needs a way to keep the job. What do you do together?

options.label: Look for a different schedule that fits the bus
options.outcome: You call about shift times that match the bus. You note what the employer says in the file.

options.label: Look for another transportation option together
options.outcome: You list other rides and who to contact. The client agrees to try one option this week.

options.label: Check if the work site has another access option
options.outcome: You review how the client gets into the site. You write down what still blocks access.

chat.text: The bus I use stopped running on my shift.
I do not know how I will get there now.

episodes.title: Updating The File
episodes.text: You sit down to close out the day. You record the client's progress toward the plan goals. You add today's narratives and correspondence to the case file.

episodes.title: Reading The Blueprint
episodes.text: You arrive at the deck with the blueprint in your hands. You trace the marks for quantities, sizes, shapes, and locations of rods. You count what you need for the first section.

episodes.title: Cutting Rods Short
episodes.text: You measure a rod against the length on the sketch. You set it in the bar cutter and cut it clean. You stack it with the others for the floor.

trial.title: Cut a rod
items: Cut the rod to length
Measure the rod to the required length
Check the cut against the required length
Set the rod in the bar cutter
trial.explain: You measure first so the cut matches the required length.

episodes.title: Setting Deck Blocks
episodes.text: You carry blocks out across the deck. You slide them under the rebar to hold the bars off the wood. You check the gap stays even as you go.

episodes.title: Tying The Same Ties
episodes.text: You sit on the mat with wire and pliers. You space rods and twist wire around each intersection. It is the same tie as yesterday, same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Setting Bars Together
episodes.text: You and your mate guide the steel mesh into the concrete form.

choice.prompt: The mesh sits uneven in the form. What do you do?

options.label: Lift and reset it flat
options.outcome: You both lift and shift the mesh flat. You fasten it down and it holds level.

options.label: Fasten it as it sits
options.outcome: You twist the fasteners in with the edge still high. It stays crooked in the form.

chat.text: This end is riding high, can you lift your side a bit?
Need to get it flat before we fasten it down.

episodes.title: Rod Spacing Off
episodes.text: You check the tied rods against the blueprint. A whole row is spaced wrong and the fastenings are tight. The concrete crew is waiting on the form.

choice.prompt: The spacing does not match the blueprint. What do you do?

options.label: Cut the ties and respacing now
options.outcome: You snip the wire and space and fasten the rods again. The pour starts late but matches the blueprint.

options.label: Leave it and keep going
options.outcome: You leave the row as tied and keep working. The wrong spacing stays in the form.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Resale / Flipping Business — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Setting Up Ventilators
episodes.text: You arrive on the unit and pick up the morning assignments. You set up the mechanical ventilator at the first bed following the specified parameters.

trial.title: Set up the ventilator
items: Start and run the ventilator following the treatment parameters
Read the specified parameters for the treatment
Set up the mechanical ventilator
Check that it is operating as ordered
trial.explain: You read the order first, then set up and run the device as specified.

episodes.title: Checking Morning Vitals
episodes.text: You do the same round of vital signs checks you did yesterday. You write down the numbers and move to the next bed. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Keeping Airway Open
episodes.text: You are called because a patient cannot breathe on their own. You prepare to perform endotracheal intubation to maintain an open airway.

choice.prompt: The patient's breathing is failing and you must decide when to intubate.

options.label: Intubate now to open the airway
options.outcome: You place the tube and the airway stays open so breathing support can continue.

options.label: Wait and recheck in a few minutes
options.outcome: You stay at the bedside and keep watching closely until you can act.

episodes.title: Helping With CPR
episodes.text: An alarm sounds and you hurry to the bedside to help with resuscitation.

choice.prompt: The patient has no pulse and you must choose what to do first.

options.label: Give artificial respiration
options.outcome: You provide breaths while the team continues chest compressions.

options.label: Assist with external cardiac massage
options.outcome: You take over compressions while another person manages the airway.

chat.text: Start artificial respiration now.
I am starting external cardiac massage.
Stay with me, keep going.

episodes.title: Updating Patient Charts
episodes.text: You sit down with the charts at the nurses' station. You enter each patient's identification and therapy information for today.

episodes.title: Watching Blood Gases
episodes.text: You check the latest vital signs, arterial blood gases, and blood chemistry. You see an adverse change and consult with the physician about it.

episodes.title: Morning Cooler Log
episodes.text: You arrive before the cooks and unlock the office. You pull out the sanitation binder and check yesterday's food temperatures. You sit down to fill in what is missing for the records.

trial.title: Spot the missing record
trial.scenario: You look at yesterday's sanitation sheet. The lunch cooler temps are filled in. The dinner cooler temps are blank and the sheet is unsigned.
options: The missing dinner temperatures and signature
The lunch temperatures that are already written
The clean binder cover on the shelf
trial.explain: The blank dinner section is what the government record still needs.

episodes.title: Counting Yesterday's Cash
episodes.text: You sit in the office and count yesterday's cash drawer. You stack the bills, roll the coins, and fill out the deposit slip. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Seating the Lunch Rush
episodes.text: You stand by the door as lunch guests come in. You pick up menus and wine lists.

choice.prompt: The window table is saved for a large party in ten minutes. What do you do?

options.label: Seat them at the next open table
options.outcome: You walk them to the next open table and hand them menus and wine lists. They sit down and start reading.

options.label: Seat them at the window anyway
options.outcome: You seat them at the window and hand them menus. You have to move the large party somewhere else when it arrives.

chat.text: Hi, table for two, please.
Can we sit by the window if it is free?
Could we see the wine list too?

episodes.title: Showing How Service Works
episodes.text: You gather the afternoon servers by the bar. You show them how you want tables greeted and checked on. You watch one round and correct the timing.

episodes.title: Checking IDs at Bar
episodes.text: You walk past the bar and see a young guest holding a beer. You stop and watch the bartender. You realize no one has checked an ID.

choice.prompt: The guest may be underage and the bartender is busy. What do you do?

options.label: Step in and check the ID now
options.outcome: You ask the guest for ID and hold the drink until you see it. The bar slows for a minute while you sort it out.

options.label: Pull the bartender aside first
options.outcome: You wave the bartender over and tell him to check the ID now. You stand there while he asks the guest for it.

episodes.title: Evening Walk Through
episodes.text: You walk the dining room again during the dinner rush. You greet new guests at the door and walk them to open seats. You hand them menus and wine lists and move on.

episodes.title: Morning Sensor Logs
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open yesterday's run files. You scroll through the sensor data and mark where the arm hesitates. You compare the signal spikes to the normal pattern.

trial.title: Find the fault
trial.scenario: The test run shows smooth joint motion on video. One sensor channel goes flat for two seconds, then comes back. The other channels stay steady through the same move.
options: The flat sensor channel needs attention first
The smooth video motion needs attention first
The steady channels need attention first
trial.explain: A flat dropout in one channel breaks the normal signal pattern.

episodes.title: Daily Backup Run
episodes.text: You plug in the drive and copy today's robot programs and parameters. You wait while the files save and check the names match yesterday's list. Same files, same folder, same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Design Review Talk
episodes.text: You sit down with a colleague to look over the new arm calculations and cost estimate. The spreadsheet is open between you.

choice.prompt: The calculations and cost estimate are in front of you. What do you do?

options.label: Approve them now
options.outcome: You sign off and your colleague sends the package on. The numbers stand as written.

options.label: Ask for a recheck of one number
options.outcome: Your colleague takes the sheet back and reruns that calculation. You review the revised sheet later.

options.label: Hold for a cost breakdown
options.outcome: Work waits until the detailed costs come in. You review them together tomorrow.

chat.text: Can you check these load numbers before I send them on?
The cost estimate went up a little with the new wrist.
Do they look right to you?

episodes.title: Bench Test Run
episodes.text: You stand at the bench with the small test robot. You load the configuration and run the application through its pick cycle. You watch each move and note where it stalls.

episodes.title: Robot Stops Mid Loop
episodes.text: You get word that the cell robot stopped mid-loop. You open the program and step through the last lines it ran. The arm repeats the same error each time you try it.

choice.prompt: The robot is stuck and the cell is waiting. What do you do first?

options.label: Step through the program line by line
options.outcome: You find the bad loop value and fix it. The robot finishes the cycle on the next try.

options.label: Reload the last good program copy
options.outcome: The robot runs again on the old settings. You still need to find the new bug later.

options.label: Stop and watch the sensor readout first
options.outcome: You see the sensor drop that trips the stop. You note it down before touching the code.

episodes.title: Filing The Approval
episodes.text: You sit back down and open the approval form. You check the design calculations and cost estimate against your notes. You sign your part and file it for the record.

episodes.title: Morning Line Check
episodes.text: You arrive and walk to the cell where an arm stopped overnight. You sit down with your meter and check the controller, sensors, and wiring. You trace the fault to a loose feedback connection.

episodes.title: Adjusting the Path
episodes.text: You stand by the teach pendant and watch the robot miss the pick by a finger width. You slow the approach and shift two points in the program. You run it again and watch it land clean.

episodes.title: Same Daily Checks
episodes.text: You walk the same line with the same checklist as yesterday. You look at the same controllers, sensors, and conveyor switches. You mark them down the same way and move on.

episodes.title: New Gripper Install
episodes.text: You kneel by the end of the arm with the operator to fit the new gripper.

choice.prompt: The gripper is mounted but the close pressure looks off. What do you do?

options.label: Reprogram the close and test it now
options.outcome: You change the program and cycle it five times. It holds firm and the run starts on time.

options.label: Leave it and watch the first run
options.outcome: You step back and watch the first parts slip again. You stop the line and fix the program anyway.

chat.text: This end-of-arm tool keeps slipping on the second shift.
Can you mount it and adjust the program before the run?
I can hold it steady while you bolt it down.

episodes.title: Arm Stops Cold
episodes.text: You get the call that a robot is dead mid-cycle. You open the cabinet and smell a burnt servo drive. The line waits while you decide the fix.

choice.prompt: The servomotor and its encoder both look bad. What do you replace first?

options.label: Swap the defective servomotor now
options.outcome: You lock out power, swap the motor, and the arm moves again. You note the encoder still needs a check later.

options.label: Swap the defective encoder first
options.outcome: You replace the encoder and power up for a test. The motor still faults, so you shut down and swap the motor next.

options.label: Replace the controller board instead
options.outcome: You change the board and test. Nothing changes, so you go back to the motor and encoder.

episodes.title: Writing Service Notes
episodes.text: You sit at the bench and open today's service records. You write down each repair, part swap, and program change. You close the log so tomorrow starts clear.

trial.title: What needs recording
trial.scenario: You check your service records at end of day. You replaced a circuit board at noon and adjusted a robot path at two. Only the path change is written down.
options: The circuit board replacement
The robot path change
The date on the page
trial.explain: The board swap is real work and the log is missing it.

episodes.title: Raising the Scaffold
episodes.text: You arrive at the house and start pinning the scaffold tubes together. You level the feet and clip in the planks like yesterday. You check the rails once and climb up the same way you always do.

episodes.title: Clearing Wet Leaves
episodes.text: You step onto the flat section with a broom and bucket. You push wet leaves and standing water toward the edge. You clear the low spot bare before any new material goes down.

episodes.title: Talking Through the Leak
episodes.text: You walk the slope with the homeowner watching from the ladder. You point out the stained shingles and soft joint.

choice.prompt: You have inspected the roof. What repair do you tell the homeowner you will do?

options.label: Patch the one joint now
options.outcome: You explain you will seal that joint today and watch the rest. She nods and asks when you can start.

options.label: Redo the larger stained section
options.outcome: You explain the wider repair and that it will take more time. She asks you to write up what it needs.

chat.text: Is it just that one corner?
What would you actually fix first?

episodes.title: Counting Materials Needed
episodes.text: You sit in the truck and measure the sketch from the morning. You count flashing strips, nails, and cement for the joints. You add up the hours for two people to finish it.

episodes.title: Sealing the Joint
episodes.text: You kneel by the chimney joint with metal strips and cement. You fit the flashing tight over the seam. You nail the edge and press cement smooth over the nail heads.

trial.title: Check the seal
trial.scenario: You have cemented the flashing strip over the joint. One nail head is left uncovered on the edge. Water sits near the seam from this morning.
options: The uncovered nail head that needs cement
The color of the metal strip
The brand of your hammer
trial.explain: An uncovered nail lets water in, so it must be sealed watertight.

episodes.title: Joint Still Leaking
episodes.text: You test the joint you sealed and water seeps under one end. You lift the edge and see the cement did not hold. You have to decide how to make it watertight before you leave.

choice.prompt: The flashing edge is still letting water in. What do you do?

options.label: Pull it and reset the strip
options.outcome: You pull the loose end, add fresh cement, and nail it flat again. The edge sits tight and the seep stops.

options.label: Add more cement over the gap
options.outcome: You press more cement into the gap and smooth it over the edge. The joint holds for now and you mark it to recheck.

episodes.title: Checking Yesterday's Files
episodes.text: You arrive early and open your filing drawer. You sit down and check yesterday's notes against district rules. You fix two missing dates before the bell rings.

episodes.title: Picking Fall Classes
episodes.text: You sit with a sophomore staring at a course sheet. You talk through class choices, schedule gaps, and study habits. She worries about failing math again.

choice.prompt: She asks to drop math for an easy elective to protect her grades. What do you do?

options.label: Keep the math class and add support
options.outcome: You keep her in math and set up weekly tutoring. She leaves with a full schedule and a plan.

options.label: Switch to the elective now
options.outcome: You change her schedule and note it in her file. She smiles, but will still need math next year.

episodes.title: Circle Talk Time
episodes.text: You pull chairs into a small circle for group time.

chat.text: I got in a fight with my best friend at lunch.
Now I don't want to come to school.
You nod and keep the group quiet to listen.

episodes.title: Same Forms Again
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk with the same attendance and record forms. You enter names, dates, and check boxes. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Hallway Crisis Call
episodes.text: A teacher flags you in the hall about a crying student.

choice.prompt: She is shaking and cannot calm down in the busy hall. What do you do first?

options.label: Move her to a quiet room with you
options.outcome: You walk her to your office and sit until her breathing slows. You stay with her until she can talk.

options.label: Ask what happened right there
options.outcome: You ask softly in the hall while students pass by. She shakes her head and covers her face.

options.label: Send her back to class to settle
options.outcome: You walk her back to class and ask the teacher to give her space. She sits down but keeps crying quietly.

chat.text: She is in room 12 and needs you now.
I can't go back to class like this.

episodes.title: Transcript and Letter
episodes.text: You sit down with a senior's transcript before she leaves. You check her credits against graduation requirements. You start her recommendation letter for college.

trial.title: Missing Credit Check
trial.scenario: You review a senior transcript for graduation. She has English, math, and electives done. She is short one required science credit to graduate.
options: Missing science credit
Missing English credit
Missing elective credit
trial.explain: Her transcript shows science is the only requirement still missing.

episodes.text: You start the main work of a School Psychologist — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: First Lesson Begins
episodes.text: You arrive before the bell and write the date on the board. You stand at the front as students sit down. You start with a short lecture to the whole group.

episodes.title: Hallway Line Check
episodes.text: You stand in the same spot by the door. You check the line is quiet and straight. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Quiet Desk Talk
episodes.text: You sit down beside a student who is falling behind after lunch.

choice.prompt: The student looks upset and class is about to restart. Do you keep talking now or set another time?

options.label: Keep listening for two more minutes
options.outcome: You stay seated and hear the rest. The student calms a little and returns to the group.

options.label: Set a time to meet later
options.outcome: You agree to meet at recess. The student nods and goes back to the desk.

chat.text: I do not get it and I feel behind.
You listen and ask what part feels hard.

episodes.title: Changing The Lesson
episodes.text: You sit at your desk with the morning pages in front of you. You see some students need a slower pace. You change the afternoon demonstration and handout to match them.

trial.title: Order the balanced lesson
items: Students try the work on their own
You show a demonstration at the front
Students ask questions and investigate what they saw
You give a short instruction to the class
trial.explain: You instruct first, then demonstrate, then let them work and investigate.

episodes.title: Loud Classroom Moment
episodes.text: You are leading a discussion when two students start shouting across the room. You stop the lesson and stand between them. The class goes quiet and waits.

choice.prompt: Both students are upset and the class is watching. What do you do first?

options.label: Restate the rule and pause the class
options.outcome: You remind them of the rule for speaking in turn. They sit down and you restart the discussion.

options.label: Move one student to work alone
options.outcome: You have one student take work to the side table. The room settles and the lesson goes on.

options.label: Give a warning and continue
options.outcome: You give a clear warning about order. They stop and you keep going with the lesson.

episodes.title: Planning Tomorrow's Work
episodes.text: You stay at your desk after the students leave. You plan tomorrow's mix of instruction, demonstration, and work time. You leave time for them to observe, question, and investigate.

episodes.title: Reading The Blueprints
episodes.text: You arrive at the house and spread the electrical layout on the hood of the van. You trace the control panel, door contacts, and camera runs with your finger. You check the plan against the rooms one more time.

episodes.title: Pulling The Cable
episodes.text: You are in the roof space with a coil of cable. You feed the run through the access hole toward the fixture outlet below. Dust hangs in your headlamp beam as you work the line through.

trial.title: Run a cable drop
items: Terminate the cable at the fixture outlet
Position the cable along the run
Feed the cable through the access hole
Work the cable through to reach the fixture outlet
trial.explain: You feed first, reach the outlet, position the slack, then terminate.

episodes.title: Mounting Panels And Sensors
episodes.text: You hold the control panel against the wall and mark your holes. You mount and fasten the panel, door contacts, and a sensor by the back window. You attach the electrical wiring to connect the components.

choice.prompt: The door frame is uneven and the contact will not sit flush. What do you do?

options.label: Shim and refit it now
options.outcome: You pack the contact out until it sits flat. It takes ten extra minutes but the magnet lines up.

options.label: Leave it loose and wire it
options.outcome: You wire it up crooked. The door shows open on the panel and you have to come back and fix it.

episodes.title: Strapping The Same Run
episodes.text: You sit in the hallway strapping cable along the same clips you did yesterday. You cut, strap, cut, strap down the whole run. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Dead Sensor Circuit
episodes.text: You test the living room circuit and the sensor shows no signal. You open the wiring spec and check the connections point by point.

choice.prompt: The meter shows a break somewhere in the loop. What do you check first?

options.label: Recheck your last terminations
options.outcome: You open the last two joints and find a loose wire. You remake it and the circuit tests good.

options.label: Swap the sensor for a new one
options.outcome: You fit a new sensor but the fault stays. You still have to open the wiring and find the break.

options.label: Jumper the zone to silence it
options.outcome: The panel goes quiet but the room is unprotected. You have to come back and repair it properly.

episodes.title: Showing The Customer
episodes.text: You walk the customer to the new keypad for the handover.

chat.text: So what sets it off by mistake?
Show her the stay mode and the entry delay.
Got it. So I need to disarm before I open the back door?

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Self-Storage Owner — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: A message lands: could you also take on one more thing today — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you?

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Focused work time — the skilled part of the day, where doing it well is the whole point. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Starting Morning Cycles
episodes.text: You arrive on the cleanroom floor and walk to your control panel. You check the valves and switches in front of you. You key in the commands to start the first semiconductor processing cycle.

choice.prompt: The panel light stays red and the cycle will not start. Do you recheck your valve and button setup or start it again anyway?

options.label: Recheck valves and buttons
options.outcome: You walk the panel again and find one valve still closed. You open it and the cycle starts clean.

options.label: Press start again
options.outcome: The panel stays red and the cycle holds. You still have to go back and check the setup.

episodes.title: Setting Furnace Controls
episodes.text: You sit down at the furnace controls with the crystal growing specs beside you. You set power level and temperature for the next run. You adjust vacuum and rotation speed until they match the sheet.

episodes.title: Grinding Polished Wafers
episodes.text: You load a batch of wafers into the grinding station. You grind, etch, and polish them to form circuitry. You watch the surface change as the conductive properties shift.

trial.title: Order the wafer steps
items: Polish the wafer to finish the surface
Load the wafer into the equipment
Etch the wafer to form circuitry
Grind the wafer to change shape
trial.explain: You load first, then etch, grind, and polish last.

episodes.title: Same Inspection Again
episodes.text: You sit at the microscope after lunch. You inspect wafers for surface defects and measure circuitry. Same check as yesterday, same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Furnace Runs Hot
episodes.text: You glance at the furnace readout and see the temperature climbing past spec.

choice.prompt: The temperature keeps rising past the crystal spec. Do you readjust the controls now or wait a few minutes?

options.label: Readjust controls now
options.outcome: You lower power and reset temperature back into spec. The run steadies and stays usable.

options.label: Wait and watch
options.outcome: The temperature climbs higher for five more minutes. You have to readjust anyway and log the drift.

options.label: Call for a second check
options.outcome: Your colleague confirms the reading while you hold the controls. You adjust together and save the run.

chat.text: Temp is drifting up. What do you see?
Vacuum still holding on my side.

episodes.title: Logging The Day
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and open the production logs. You enter processing, production, and inspection information for today. You save the reports and close out your shift.

episodes.title: Getting Out of Bed
episodes.text: You arrive and pull back the blanket. You sit Mrs. Lee up slow and help her swing her feet to the floor.

trial.title: What Needs Attention
trial.scenario: You help Mrs. Lee sit up to get out of bed for dressing. Her foot is caught in the blanket, her morning pill cup sits untouched, and the sheet is damp.
options: Free her caught foot before moving her
Hand her the pill cup right away
Change the damp sheet first
trial.explain: You clear what would trip or hurt her before anything else.

episodes.title: Morning Bath Help
episodes.text: You run the bath and help her in to wash.

choice.prompt: The bath water feels too hot for her. What do you do?

options.label: Add cool water and test it
options.outcome: You add cool water and check it with your hand. She nods and settles back in.

options.label: Help her in anyway
options.outcome: She flinches and grips your arm. You stop and run the water cooler.

chat.text: Oh, that's too hot for me.
Can we cool it down a little?

episodes.title: Sheets and Laundry
episodes.text: You strip the bed and put on fresh linens. You wash the laundry, iron what needs it, and wipe the room. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Midday Pills
episodes.text: You read the written directions from the nurse. You hand him the oral pills with water and stay until he swallows them.

episodes.title: Stuck in Chair
episodes.text: You go to help Mr. Diaz move from his wheelchair to the bed. He slips halfway up and grabs your arm hard. He looks scared and will not move.

choice.prompt: He is half up and frozen, holding your arm. What do you do?

options.label: Ease him back into the chair
options.outcome: You lower him slowly back into the seat. He breathes out and sits safe.

options.label: Keep lifting him to the bed
options.outcome: He stiffens and slides a little. You stop and settle him back down.

options.label: Hold still and talk him through it
options.outcome: You stay steady and wait with him. After a minute he lets you guide him down.

episodes.title: Notes for Nurse
episodes.text: You sit down and write up care, condition, and progress for the day. You note the bath, the pills taken, and the trouble with the chair move.

episodes.title: Checking Yesterday's Numbers
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open yesterday's dashboard. You look at visits, time on site, and click-through rates. You note page views per visit are down.

trial.title: Spot what needs attention
trial.scenario: You review the morning metrics. Visits are steady, but time on site fell and conversion rate dropped on one landing page.
options: Ignore the dip and move on
Flag the landing page conversion drop first
Report only total visits
trial.explain: You flag the conversion drop first because it shows real loss on that page.

episodes.title: Fixing Pages for Search
episodes.text: You open a product page with heavy graphics and long text. You compress the images and tighten the headings for search and display. You check how it loads on your phone.

episodes.title: Updating the Tracker
episodes.text: You open the same search tracking sheet you update every day. You paste in visits, clicks, and cost per click. You save it and close it.

episodes.title: Planning Online Strategy
episodes.text: You sit down with marketing to talk through the online strategy. Your boss messages about where to place keywords next.

choice.prompt: The team asks where to focus keyword placement in the strategy. What do you suggest?

options.label: Keep the old pages as-is
options.outcome: You keep the old pages running. Traffic stays flat for the next week.

options.label: Shift keywords to the new guides
options.outcome: You move keywords and links to the new guides. You watch the clicks shift over the next few days.

chat.text: We need to decide where to push content this month. What are you seeing in search patterns?
I say we keep spending on the old landing pages.

episodes.title: Traffic Drop Alert
episodes.text: You see search traffic fall sharply after a change in search engine patterns. You pull keyword rankings and check placement. You need to act before the day ends.

choice.prompt: One key page lost most of its search placement. What do you do first?

options.label: Rewrite the page keywords now
options.outcome: You update the keywords and headings. You submit the page and wait for it to be reindexed.

options.label: Wait and watch until tomorrow
options.outcome: You leave the page alone overnight. The low placement and low visits continue.

options.label: Redirect traffic from another page
options.outcome: You add links from a stronger page. Some visits flow back while you plan the fix.

episodes.title: Sending the Daily Report
episodes.text: You pull together tracking on search activity and web metrics. You write a short analysis of visits, transaction volume, and cost per acquisition. You send it to the marketing executives.

episodes.title: Morning Truck Roll
episodes.text: You arrive at the yard and climb into the truck. You check the crew, materials, and equipment in the back. You drive out toward the work site.

episodes.title: Manhole Check First
episodes.text: You lift the manhole cover and look inside with your light. You watch how the water sits and moves. You mark where the line looks stopped.

trial.title: Spot the Stoppage
trial.scenario: You look into two open manholes. The upstream one is full and still. The downstream one is low and flowing.
options: The upstream manhole with still, high water
The dry grass beside the road
The clean truck bed
trial.explain: High still water upstream points to a stoppage below it.

episodes.title: Running the Flusher
episodes.text: You stand by the sewer flusher and run the same pass again. You watch the hose feed out and pull back. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Radio Call Update
episodes.text: You park by the curb and answer the wireless phone. Your supervisor wants an update on the stoppage.

choice.prompt: Your supervisor asks if you need another worker on site. What do you say?

options.label: Ask him to send another worker
options.outcome: You tell him you need help. He says a worker will drive out after lunch.

options.label: Tell him you can finish with the crew you have
options.outcome: You tell him you are fine. You hang up and get back to the line.

chat.text: Where are you on that line?
Do you need me to send another worker?
Let me know what you ran so far.

episodes.title: Line Backing Up
episodes.text: You run the power rodder and it stops hard in the line. Water starts backing up toward the manhole rim. You shut the feed and step back.

choice.prompt: The rod is stuck and water is rising. What do you do next?

options.label: Pull the rod back and try the high-velocity water jet
options.outcome: You ease the rod out and set up the jet. You run water through to clear the blockage.

options.label: Call your supervisor on the radio telephone
options.outcome: You call and describe the backup. He tells you to hold and wait for direction.

episodes.title: Writing the Log
episodes.text: You sit in the truck cab with your work sheet. You write down what you inspected and what you ran. You note the maintenance and repair work for the record.
